story_description: Create the foundational data model, builder, view model, and UI components for representing hook execution events in a timeline/Gantt chart format, enabling visualization of hook lifecycles with proper temporal relationships, hierarchical structure, and interactive exploration.
task_description: Create the HookTooltip SwiftUI view that displays comprehensive hook execution details on hover, including hook name, type, duration, status, input/output preview, environment variables used, and error details if applicable. The tooltip appears on mouse hover over Gantt bars and rows.
atom_description: Implement the HookTooltip SwiftUI view component that renders a floating popover-style tooltip when hovering over GanttBar or GanttRow elements. The tooltip displays: hook name with icon, execution status with color indicator, start time formatted as HH:mm:ss.SSS, duration in human-readable format (e.g., 142ms, 1.2s), hook type badge (command/prompt), input JSON preview (first 200 chars), output/result preview (first 200 chars), environment variables accessed, and error message with stack trace preview for failed hooks. Uses NSPopover on macOS for native tooltip behavior with smooth fade animations.
problem_statement: When users view the Gantt timeline, they can see hook execution bars with colors indicating status, but they lack detailed context about what each hook actually did. Users need to hover over a bar to see: what hook ran, how long it took, what input it received, what output it produced, which environment variables it accessed, and why it failed (if applicable). Without tooltips, users must navigate away from the Gantt view to inspect individual hook details, breaking their flow and reducing the utility of the visualization.

assumptions: HookTimelineEvent model includes all necessary data: name, status, startTime, endTime, and associated HookExecution for I/O data
NSPopover is available on macOS for native tooltip rendering with arrow pointing to source
SwiftUI onHover modifier works reliably on macOS for hover detection
Mouse position can be tracked via NSEvent.mouseLocation for tooltip positioning
HookExecution model provides access to input JSON, output JSON, environment variables accessed, and error details
System appearance (light/dark) can be detected via colorScheme environment value
Tooltip should not persist when mouse leaves the source element (no delay before hiding)
constraints: Must use NSPopover for macOS-native tooltip behavior rather than SwiftUI overlay (better positioning and arrow)
Tooltip width must not exceed 320pt to fit on smaller displays
Input/output preview must truncate at 200 characters with ellipsis to prevent massive tooltips
Tooltip must appear within 150ms of hover to feel responsive
Tooltip must dismiss immediately when mouse leaves (no linger delay)
Must work correctly when Gantt view is scrolled (tooltip tracks source element position)
Must not block interaction with other UI elements when visible
VoiceOver must read tooltip content when GanttBar is focused
functional_requirements: FR1: HookTooltip shall accept a HookTimelineEvent and optional HookExecution as input data sources
FR2: HookTooltip header section shall display hook name in bold 13pt font with status icon (checkmark/x/spinner) and colored status label (green=completed, red=failed, blue=running, gray=pending)
FR3: HookTooltip timing section shall display start time formatted as HH:mm:ss.SSS and duration in human-readable format (ms for <1s, s with 1 decimal for <60s, m:ss for >=60s)
FR4: HookTooltip type section shall display hook type badge (Command or Prompt) with appropriate icon (terminal or brain SF Symbol)
FR5: HookTooltip input section shall display JSON preview of hook input truncated to 200 characters with monospace font and syntax highlighting for keys
FR6: HookTooltip output section shall display hook output/result truncated to 200 characters, or 'No output' placeholder if empty
FR7: HookTooltip environment section shall list environment variables accessed by the hook (e.g., CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, HOME) if available from HookExecution metadata
FR8: HookTooltip error section shall only appear when status is failed, displaying error message and first 3 lines of stack trace
FR9: HookTooltip shall fade in over 200ms with ease-out timing when appearing
FR10: HookTooltip shall fade out over 150ms when dismissing
FR11: HookTooltip shall position itself near the mouse cursor with arrow pointing to source GanttBar
FR12: HookTooltip shall reposition to avoid clipping screen edges (flip arrow direction if needed)
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Tooltip shall appear within 150ms of hover event to feel responsive
NFR2: Tooltip rendering shall not cause frame drops (maintain 60fps during animation)
NFR3: Memory usage per tooltip instance shall not exceed 5KB excluding cached images
NFR4: Tooltip shall support dynamic type sizes for accessibility (respecting system font size preference)
NFR5: Tooltip content shall be readable by VoiceOver in logical order: name, status, timing, type, input, output, errors
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookTooltip.swift in Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Define HookTooltipContent struct to encapsulate all displayable data extracted from HookTimelineEvent and HookExecution
Step 3: Create HookTooltipContentBuilder that extracts and formats data: truncates strings, formats dates, determines visibility of sections
Step 4: Define HookTooltip view struct with @State for animation, @Environment for colorScheme
Step 5: Implement header section with HStack containing status icon (SF Symbol), name text (bold), and status label (colored)
Step 6: Implement timing section with VStack containing start time label and duration label with clock icon
Step 7: Implement type badge section using Capsule background with hook type text and icon
Step 8: Implement input preview section with Text view using monospace font, lineLimit(5), and truncation
Step 9: Implement output preview section with similar styling to input, or placeholder text if empty
Step 10: Implement environment section with ForEach over environment variable names in gray monospace
Step 11: Implement error section with conditional visibility based on status, showing error message in red and stack trace preview in monospace
Step 12: Wrap all sections in VStack with 12pt spacing and padding(12)
Step 13: Create HookTooltipPopover wrapper that manages NSPopover lifecycle and positioning
Step 14: Implement showTooltip(for:at:) method that creates and presents NSPopover at specified screen location
Step 15: Implement hideTooltip() method that closes NSPopover with fade animation
Step 16: Add onHover modifier integration point for GanttBar and GanttRow to trigger tooltip show/hide
Step 17: Implement edge detection logic to flip tooltip arrow direction when near screen boundaries
Step 18: Add VoiceOver accessibility labels to all sections using accessibilityLabel modifier
Step 19: Write unit tests for HookTooltipContentBuilder formatting logic
Step 20: Write UI tests verifying tooltip appears on hover and contains expected content
data_model_changes: New struct HookTooltipContent with properties: name (String), statusIcon (String), statusLabel (String), statusColor (Color), startTime (String), duration (String), hookType (String), hookTypeIcon (String), inputPreview (String?), outputPreview (String?), environmentVariables ([String]), errorMessage (String?), stackTracePreview (String?)
No changes to existing data models; HookTooltipContent is derived/computed from HookTimelineEvent and HookExecution
api_contracts: HookTooltip.init(event: HookTimelineEvent, execution: HookExecution?) - primary initializer
HookTooltipContentBuilder.build(from event: HookTimelineEvent, execution: HookExecution?) -> HookTooltipContent - factory method
HookTooltipPopover.shared: HookTooltipPopover - singleton accessor for tooltip manager
HookTooltipPopover.show(content: HookTooltipContent, at: CGPoint, relativeTo: NSView) - present tooltip
event_contracts: TooltipShown: Emitted when tooltip becomes visible, payload: { eventId: UUID, hookName: String }
TooltipDismissed: Emitted when tooltip is hidden, payload: { eventId: UUID, dwellTime: TimeInterval }
ui_states: Hidden: Default state, no tooltip visible, waiting for hover event
Appearing: Fade-in animation in progress (200ms), tooltip content rendered but opacity animating from 0 to 1
Visible: Fully opaque, positioned near source element, content displayed
Disappearing: Fade-out animation in progress (150ms), opacity animating from 1 to 0, then transitions to Hidden
ui_interactions: Hover over GanttBar: After 100ms dwell time, trigger TooltipShown event and transition to Appearing state
Mouse leave GanttBar: Immediately trigger TooltipDismissed event and transition to Disappearing state
Scroll Gantt view while tooltip visible: Reposition tooltip to track source element, or dismiss if element scrolls out of view
Focus GanttBar via keyboard: Show tooltip and announce content via VoiceOver
Press Escape while tooltip visible: Dismiss tooltip immediately
ui_copy: Empty state placeholders: 'No output', 'No input data', 'No environment variables accessed'
Truncation indicator: ' [truncated]' appended to truncated content
edge_cases: Edge case 1: HookExecution is nil (only HookTimelineEvent available) - show basic info (name, status, timing) without I/O preview sections
Edge case 2: Input JSON is empty string or null - show 'No input data' placeholder
Edge case 3: Output JSON exceeds 200 characters - truncate and append ' [truncated]' suffix
Edge case 4: Hook is still running (no endTime) - show 'Running' status with spinner icon, duration shows elapsed time
Edge case 5: Error message exceeds 500 characters - truncate error message at 500 chars with ellipsis
Edge case 6: Stack trace has more than 3 lines - show first 3 lines with '+ N more lines' suffix
Edge case 7: Mouse moves rapidly between multiple GanttBars - dismiss previous tooltip immediately before showing new one (no overlap)
Edge case 8: GanttBar near right edge of screen - flip tooltip to appear on left side with arrow pointing right
Edge case 9: GanttBar near bottom edge of screen - flip tooltip to appear above with arrow pointing down
Edge case 10: System in dark mode - tooltip background uses dark popover appearance, text uses light colors
Edge case 11: Environment variables array is empty - hide environment section entirely rather than showing empty list
Edge case 12: Hook type is unknown/future type - display type as-is without icon, fallback to generic tag icon
failure_modes: FM1: NSPopover fails to create (rare AppKit issue) - log error and silently fail, user sees no tooltip but app continues functioning
FM2: HookExecution data is corrupted or has invalid JSON - catch decoding error, show tooltip with available data and 'Data unavailable' in I/O sections
FM3: Mouse position tracking fails - use fallback position centered on GanttBar bounds rather than mouse cursor
FM4: Animation frame drops due to heavy concurrent processing - skip animation and show tooltip immediately at full opacity
FM5: VoiceOver not running but accessibility labels still computed - no impact, labels ignored when VoiceOver inactive
FM6: Tooltip content builder throws unexpected error - wrap in do-catch, return minimal tooltip with name and status only
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/UI/Hooks/HookTooltip.swift. Remove onHover modifier calls from GanttBar.swift and GanttRow.swift that reference HookTooltipPopover. Gantt visualization continues to work without tooltips - users see bars but no hover details. No data migration required. No other features affected.

risks: Risk 1: NSPopover positioning may be incorrect on external displays with different scaling
Risk 2: Rapid hover between bars could cause tooltip flicker or overlap
Risk 3: Large input/output JSON could cause layout issues even with truncation
Risk 4: VoiceOver announcement order may not match visual layout
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Test on multiple display configurations and use screen-relative coordinates from NSScreen.main
Mitigation 2: Implement debounce (100ms) before showing new tooltip and cancel pending show when mouse moves
Mitigation 3: Enforce strict maxWidth(320) and use fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true) for text wrapping
Mitigation 4: Use accessibilityElement(children: .combine) and explicit accessibilitySortPriority to control reading order
risk_register.blast_radius: Low - tooltip is additive UX enhancement only. Failure hides tooltip but Gantt visualization remains fully functional. No data loss or core functionality impact. Users can still click bars to navigate to detail views.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If NSPopover proves problematic, fallback to SwiftUI .popover modifier with custom positioning logic. This loses the native arrow but maintains functionality. If all tooltip approaches fail, remove hover handling from GanttBar/GanttRow and document that detailed info requires click navigation.
